why: componentName is fully caller-controlled per the tool's own schema (free-form string, no length cap in the schema itself) and is traced all the way from handleGetComponentMetadata -> axios.getComponentMetadata -> the RegExp constructor with zero escaping. A value containing a classic catastrophic-backtracking sub-pattern (nested/overlapping quantifiers) makes the resulting regex exhibit exponential-time backtracking against the multi-KB registry file content, tying up the Node event loop -- a targeted availability mechanism (ReDoS), not a generic malformed-input crash. This was reasoned statically from the code per the task's no-execute rule; I did not actually run the server to time the hang.

why: handleGetDirectoryStructure (src/tools/repository/get-directory-structure.ts:5-25) passes owner/repo/path/branch straight through to axios.buildDirectoryTree with only '|| default' fallbacks, never enforcing that owner/repo stay pinned to shadcn-ui/ui as the tool's description implies. A caller can therefore point this tool at any owner/repo/branch/path on api.github.com. If the deployer set GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN (optional, for higher rate limits), that credential is silently reused for the caller-chosen repo, letting the tool be used to browse repos the token can see beyond shadcn-ui/ui. I could not confirm from static code whether a given deployment actually has that token configured, which is why this is Tier B rather than A.
